title.rendered: Nicodemus by Night: You Must Be Born Again: The Gospel For Today

excerpt.rendered: “Unless one is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.” A morning devotional on the new birth every religious heart still needs.

content.rendered:
It was night in Jerusalem when the Pharisee Nicodemus made his way to the young Galilean rabbi. He came under cover of darkness because he could not afford to be seen. And in that midnight conversation Jesus spoke one of the most transforming sentences of His entire earthly ministry.

The Gospel For Today | Monday, September 7, 2026

Today’s Scripture

“Jesus answered and said to him, ‘Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.'”
John 3:3 (NKJV)

Today’s Message

It was night in Jerusalem when the Pharisee Nicodemus made his way to the young Galilean rabbi who had come to town for the Passover feast. Nicodemus was not a marginal figure. He was a member of the Sanhedrin, the seventy-one-member ruling council that oversaw Jewish religious life. He was a teacher of Israel. He had the education, the respectability, the standing, and the reputation. He also had a growing conviction that this Jesus of Nazareth was from God. But he could not afford to be seen with Him publicly. So he came at night, quietly, alone, up whatever stairs led to the room where Jesus was staying. And in the darkness of that first meeting, Jesus spoke one of the most transforming sentences of His entire earthly ministry.

“Most assuredly, I say to you, unless one is born again, he cannot see the kingdom of God.” Nicodemus had come with a compliment. “Rabbi, we know that You are a teacher come from God.” Jesus does not receive the compliment and expand it into a polite discussion. He goes straight to the heart of the matter. Religion, education, moral achievement, tradition, respectability, all of it, cannot get a person into the Kingdom. Only a new birth can. And the new birth is not something the seeker manufactures. It is something the Spirit of God does, from above, in a life that has been surrendered to Jesus.

The Greek phrase Jesus uses for “born again” is gennēthē anōthen. The word anōthen can mean “again” or “from above.” Both meanings are present, and both are theologically loaded. The believer is born again, from above, by the Spirit of God. It is not a self-improvement. It is not a fresh resolution. It is not a religious ritual. It is a new life, given from above, planted in a heart that could not have generated it on its own.

The Passion Translation opens up the weight of what Jesus is saying: “Jesus answered, ‘Nicodemus, listen to this eternal truth: Without being born from above, no one is able to experience the reality of God’s kingdom'” (John 3:3 TPT). The Amplified Bible Classic Edition adds: “I assure you, most solemnly I tell you, that unless a person is born again (anew, from above), he cannot ever see (know, be acquainted with, and experience) the kingdom of God” (John 3:3 AMPC). See. Know. Be acquainted with. Experience. The Kingdom is not an idea to grasp intellectually. It is a reality to enter. And the entrance is by new birth.

John gives us Nicodemus in three snapshots across his gospel. In chapter 3, he comes at night, confused and questioning. In chapter 7, he stands up in the Sanhedrin and speaks a small defence of Jesus, arguing that Jesus should be given a fair hearing under Jewish law. In chapter 19, after the crucifixion, he brings a hundred pounds of myrrh and aloes and helps Joseph of Arimathea bury the body of Jesus. Nicodemus becomes a follower. The midnight conversation on the rooftop was not the end. It was the beginning. For Gospelbuzz readers today, wherever you are reading this from, in Lagos or London or Manila or Nairobi or Sao Paulo, take heart if your first steps toward Jesus have felt tentative and hidden. The seed of new life planted in the darkness is still the seed of new life. He who is born again from above will one day, publicly, stand with the crucified Christ. Come to Jesus in whatever posture you have today. He will meet you where you are.

Prayer

Father, I acknowledge that I was born again from above by Your Spirit through faith in Christ. My new life is not something I manufactured. It was Your gift. Today I honour the miracle of the new birth in my life. I refuse to try to earn what You have already freely given. I walk today as one born from above, seeing the Kingdom, entering the Kingdom, belonging to the King. And I pray for those who are still coming to Jesus at night, tentative and hidden. Meet them where they are. Grow in them the seed of new life. In Jesus’ name. Amen.

Declaration

I am born again from above by the Spirit of God. My new life is a gift. I see the Kingdom. I enter the Kingdom. I belong to the King.
